jobs.title: Technical Product Manager
jobs.description:
Swarm Aero is redefining air power, building the largest swarming UAV and the most versatile swarming aircraft network in the world. The company is moving quickly to launch the first aircraft designed specifically for swarming, as well as the Command & Control software to mobilize swarms of thousands of heterogeneous autonomous assets and empower human operators to achieve superhuman results.

The team has created and exited multiple startups, negotiated defense deals worth billions of dollars, and designed and built 30+ novel aircraft, with aerospace experience from Scaled Composites, Airbus, Archer Aviation, Blue Origin, and Boom Supersonic.

Mission

Turn operational needs, customer feedback, and product direction into clear product specifications—and then drive those capabilities through decisions, design, development, and validation.

You will work directly with the Head of Product on Legion and become a core contributor to both defining the product and running the process around it.

What You’ll Own

  • Create clear, detailed product specifications for new features and capabilities.

  • Take customer needs, operator feedback, technical constraints, and product direction and turn them into actionable product requirements.

  • Own bounded features from early definition through design, development, feedback, and validation.

  • Work directly with Product Design to translate specifications into detailed workflows and Figma designs.

  • Review designs and implementations against product intent and requirements.

  • Facilitate product discussions with government customers, third-party contractors, operators, engineers, and internal stakeholders.

  • Prepare agendas and clearly identify topics requiring feedback, decisions, or alignment.

  • Capture decisions, unresolved issues, customer feedback, and action items.

  • Incorporate meeting outcomes directly into product specifications and related artifacts.

  • Maintain feature status, decision history, feedback registers, and key product commitments.

  • Identify ambiguity, conflicting requirements, and missing decisions before they slow the team down.

  • Track important product and contractual deliverables.

  • Help prepare product reviews, demonstrations, and customer discussions.

  • Create enough structure to keep the organization aligned without introducing unnecessary process.

What Great Looks Like

You are given a problem such as:

“Operators need a better way to understand and respond to vehicle health issues during degraded communications.”

You meet with the relevant operators, engineers, customers, and stakeholders.

You understand the underlying problem.

You separate customer requests from actual product requirements.

You identify edge cases and unresolved decisions.

You write a product specification that clearly explains the intended behavior, workflows, system states, requirements, and open questions.

You work with Product Design to turn that specification into a strong interface.

You incorporate feedback, resolve ambiguity, and keep the feature moving until the capability works as intended.

The Head of Product provides direction and reviews the most important decisions—but does not need to personally produce every artifact or manage every follow-up.

Early Expectations

Within the first few weeks, you should begin contributing directly to product specifications.

Initially, you may draft sections of specifications or own smaller, well-bounded capabilities with guidance from the Head of Product.

As your understanding of Legion, its operators, and the technical architecture grows, you will rapidly take ownership of larger features.

We are not looking for someone who spends six months observing before contributing.

The Person We’re Looking For

You are an excellent writer.

You can take a complicated conversation and turn it into a clear product definition.

You have strong product judgment and are comfortable making reasonable decisions when requirements are incomplete.

You understand that a customer request is not automatically a product requirement.

You are technically curious and capable of participating meaningfully in discussions with software engineers, systems engineers, operators, and external partners.

You naturally ask questions like:

  • What problem are we actually trying to solve?

  • Who needs this capability?

  • What should happen in this edge case?

  • What does the operator see?

  • What state is the system actually in?

  • How will we know this works?

  • Is this a product decision, an engineering decision, or a customer preference?

  • You are highly organized, but organization is a means to an end.

  • Your real job is creating clarity and moving product decisions forward.

Particularly Valuable Experience

Experience with any of the following would be especially valuable:

  • Technical product management

  • Complex B2B software

  • Command-and-control systems

  • Aerospace or defense

  • Robotics or autonomous systems

  • Mission planning

  • Geospatial software

  • Systems engineering

  • Government programs

  • Operational testing

  • Requirements development

What This Role Is Not

This is not a project coordinator role.

It is not a Scrum Master role.

It is not an administrative Product Operations position.

It is not someone whose primary contribution is scheduling meetings, maintaining Jira, or writing meeting minutes.

Those activities may occasionally be necessary, but they are secondary.

The primary contribution is:

understanding product problems and defining excellent solutions.

Success After 90 Days

  • You are independently drafting product specifications for bounded Legion features.

  • Customer and operator feedback is consistently translated into clear product requirements.

  • Product meetings result in updated specifications, decisions, and actionable follow-up.

  • The Head of Product can delegate meaningful feature-definition work to you.

  • Product Design receives clearer inputs and can move faster.

  • Important product decisions and rationale are documented and traceable.

jobs.title: Senior Backend Engineer
jobs.description:
About Payflows

At Payflows, we build software that helps large companies manage and automate their payment workflows. It’s not the flashiest part of a business, but it’s one of the most critical: invoices, approvals, payments, and controls. When these things slow down, the whole company feels it.

But our ambition goes further than just building a better workflow tool.

We believe the future of finance operations is not faster clicking: it’s no clicking at all 🫳 🎤

Finance teams shouldn’t spend their days moving data from one screen to another. Software should do the operational work, and humans should focus on reviewing, approving, and making the decisions that matter.

That’s the direction we’re building toward: an agent-driven finance platform, where intelligent agents handle the repetitive tasks, and users stay in control.

We started in 2022 with a small team and a rough first version of the product. Three years later, we’re working with major companies across France, the UK, and the US while choosing to keep our team small and human-sized.

We moved fast, shipped a lot, and not everything was built in a perfect way. But it helped us learn quickly, sign real customers, and prove that the problem we’re solving truly matters.

In 2024, investors trusted us with a $25M Series A. That gives us the chance to keep growing while also strengthening our foundations and building the system that will power this agent-driven future.

Today, we’re about 35 people from many different countries, and we’re looking for a few amazing humans to join the next chapter. 🤗

🚀 What you’ll actually do

You’ll help build a product that real finance teams rely on every day.

For us, engineering is not just about clean code, it’s about reliability, clarity, and trust, especially when money and automation are involved.

In a typical week, you might:

  • Design and implement new services for a product feature.

  • Refactor an early service to make it more robust.

  • Investigate a performance or production issue.

  • Work with product and frontend to shape a new feature.

  • Review code and help teammates improve.

  • Build backend tools that our AI agents use to perform real finance operations.

  • Design safe, deterministic workflows where agents propose actions and humans review them.

Your time will be split between building new features and improving what already exists. Both matter.

You won’t just build endpoints. You’ll help shape the execution layer that our agents rely on: the APIs, data models, and workflows that let them act safely in production.

You’ll work closely with product, frontend, and customer-facing teams. We expect engineers to take ownership of parts of the system and help make them more reliable over time.

💻 Our current tech reality

Our stack evolves based on our challenges, but we care more about good design than trendy tools 🙏

Python is our core language. It helps us move fast, keep the code readable, and fits naturally with our AI-driven approach. A growing part of the system is built around agents that use our backend as a set of reliable, deterministic tools.

  • Core language: Python

  • Backend: FastAPI + Pydantic

  • Data: PostgreSQL

  • Infra: AWS, serverless when it makes sense

  • Performance: some Rust for critical paths

  • Architecture: multi-service backend, simple enough to reason about

Some parts of the system are clean and well-tested. Others were built quickly and need love. That’s the phase we’re in.

Over the next year, we’ll focus on:

  • Turning core workflows into reliable tools for our agents

  • Simplifying services

  • Improving tests and observability

  • Making performance more predictable

  • Cleaning up early code

We know we’re not perfect, but we care a lot about improving step by step.


✨ Who’s going to thrive with us

You’ll probably feel comfortable here if:

  • You like building products people actually use.

  • You are autonomous and take ownership of what you ship.

  • You take initiative and lead by example.

  • You’re curious and enjoy figuring things out.

  • You’re pragmatic about trade-offs.

  • You communicate with kindness and clarity.

This role is a great fit if you’re excited by the idea of:

  • Building systems that are used by AI agents, not just humans.

  • Designing reliable, safe automation in production.

  • Working on a product that is still early and evolving quickly.

You don’t need to know everything about AI. But you should be curious about it and excited to work in a system where agents are part of the core product 🤖

🧩 What you’ll get from this role

  • Real ownership over parts of the system.

  • Direct impact on customers and product decisions.

  • A small, human team where your work is visible and meaningful 🤝

  • A mix of feature work, system design, and technical improvements.

  • Exposure to real scaling and production challenges.

  • The chance to help build an agent-driven product from the inside.

We offer:

  • Competitive salary and equity.

  • Flexible remote setup (we prefer people to come into Paris or London office twice per week. At a minimum we’d ask you to be at an office 3 days per month, onboard in Paris for your first few weeks, and work CEST timezone).

  • A high-autonomy environment where you have real ownership and space to make an impact.

  • Plenty of room to grow, take responsibility, and shape parts of the product.

  • A culture based on trust, ownership, and clear communication.

This isn’t a huge corporate environment. In exchange, you get autonomy, responsibility, and the chance to shape a product that’s still early in its story—and help build what finance operations will look like in the next decade 🚀

Students explore the topic through research, interviews and real enterprise cases (month 1), classify goals, talent profiles and success patterns (month 2), and build strategy blueprints, a final report and a pitch to Mediacharge leadership (month 3). Students are fascinated by marketing at international enterprise scale, work analytically and build things that hold up in practice. Strong results open the door to a next conversation with Mediacharge.
